chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Daylamī, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Madāʾinī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him, “May I be made your ransom, inform me about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:”

“The only recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive in the land spreading corruption is that they be killed, or crucified, or that their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides, or that they be banished from the land.”

He said: then he counted on his hand and said, “O Abā ʿAbd Allāh, take it as four for four.” Then he said, “If he wages war against Allah and His Messenger and strives in the land spreading corruption, then kills, he is killed. If he kills and takes property, he is killed and crucified. If he takes property and does not kill, his hand and foot are cut off on opposite sides. And if he wages war against Allah and strives in the land spreading corruption, but does not kill and does not take any property, he is banished in the land.”

He said: I said, “And what is the limit of his banishment?” He said, “One year: he is banished from the land in which he committed it to another land. Then a letter is written to that town that he is banished, so do not eat with him, do not drink with him, and do not marry him, until he leaves for another place. Then a letter is written to them also with the like of that. This remains his condition for one year. When that has been done to him, he repents while humbled.”

key_terms.تُقَطَّعَ: that they be cut off; referring here to cutting the hand and foot on opposite sides
key_terms.صَاغِرٌ: humbled; brought low through the enforcement of the penalty
key_terms.فَسَادًا: corruption; grave criminal disorder and destructive wrongdoing in the land
key_terms.مَنْفِيٌّ: banished person; one formally exiled and identified as such to others
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: they wage war; here, those who violently oppose lawful order in a way treated as muḥārabah
key_terms.يُصَلَّبُوا: that they be crucified; a punishment mentioned for the one who kills and takes property
key_terms.يُقَتَّلُوا: that they be killed; the penalty for one form of the offense
key_terms.يُنْفَوْا: that they be banished; exile from the land as a prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Quranic punishments for muḥārabah and spreading corruption in the land?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse concerning those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land by matching four punishments to four forms of criminal conduct. It clarifies that the ruling varies according to whether the offender killed, took property, did both, or did neither, and it defines banishment as a one-year social and territorial exclusion.
